story.headline: No. 9 Texas Tech wants more than 10-win seasons with another Big 12 title game in reach vs. TCU
paragraphs: No. 9 Texas Tech has already clinched consecutive 10-win seasons for the first time in school history, though that isn't how coach Joey McGuire views success for his Red Raiders a year after winning the Big 12 championship and making the College Football Playoff.

“Success to me looks like going back to the Big 12 championship game, winning it and finding a way to win in the playoffs,” McGuire said this week. “It's going to look totally different than what I imagined in January what it would look like. But these guys have found a way.”

The Red Raiders (10-1, 7-1 Big 12, No. 11 CFP) take a school-record 14-game home winning streak into Thursday night's game against TCU (5-6, 3-5), which just fired coach Sonny Dykes. Another win puts them in the conference championship game against No. 2 Utah (11-0, 8-0, No. 2 CFP) on Dec. 4, when the winner is guaranteed a spot in the 12-team playoff field.
Texas Tech lost 23-0 loss to Oregon in the CFP quarterfinal at the Orange Bowl last year after a No. 4 final ranking and first-round bye.

story.headline: No. 1 Georgia is looking to extend 8-game winning streak against Georgia Tech in state rivalry
paragraphs: Georgia coach Kirby Smart has no shortage of recent evidence that the No. 1 Bulldogs cannot overlook their rivalry game against Georgia Tech on Saturday.

Georgia (10-1, No. 1 CFP) has won its last eight games against Georgia Tech (3-8), but each of the last three has been a one-possession game. That includes Georgia's 44-42 win in eight overtimes in 2024, the last time the game was played in Athens. The Bulldogs escaped with a 16-9 win over the Yellow Jackets last year in the rivalry known as “Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate.”
“A lot of hatred in that game," said Georgia tight end Ethan Barbour. “It’s always fun to play them every year. We play them hard, they play us hard. So, I mean, it’s gonna be a good game.”

It has been a tough season for Georgia Tech coach Brent Key, who fired defensive coordinator Jason Semore and three other assistants on Nov. 7. The Yellow Jackets are tied for last place in the Atlantic Coast Conference at 2-6 with no bowl game coming while Georgia will play in the Southeastern Conference championship game on Dec. 5 in Atlanta as a national title favorite.

story.headline: College football Week 13: USC-UCLA tops schedule with conference title game spots, CFP bids at stake

Things get started Thanksgiving night when TCU, with defensive coordinator Andy Avalos the interim coach following Sonny Dykes' firing, visits a No. 9 Texas Tech team going for its fifth straight win and a spot opposite No. 2 Utah in the Big 12 title game.

Nebraska, which just ended its 31-game losing streak against Top 25 opponents, will go on the road Friday and try to put a hole in No. 13 Iowa's CFP hopes. No. 5 Texas, still alive for the Southeastern Conference championship game, visits down-and-out rival Texas A&M and will go for a fourth straight win in the series. story.headline: No. 7 Tennessee looks for win over Vanderbilt to help lock down CFP game, perhaps at home
paragraphs: The seventh-ranked Tennessee Volunteers have put themselves in position to make some program history on Saturday night.
Beating in-state rival Vanderbilt should earn the Vols their second berth in three seasons in the College Football Playoffs. That would also put hosting that game at Neyland Stadium within reach.

With a little bit of help. the Vols also could earn a spot in the Southeastern Conference championship game title Dec. 5 with their third 10-win season in five years. Coach Josh Heupel wants Tennessee (9-2, 6-2, No. 5 CFP) focusing on what the Vols can control.

“There’s a lot of outside noise at this point in the year, but that’s the way you want it,” Heupel said. "It means you’ve done the right things throughout the course of the year. But for us, pay no attention to it. It’s about preparation, practicing well and getting prepared to go play your best football. Our job is to win on Saturday, and that’s it.”

story.headline: Resurgent Auburn tries to end a 6-game skid against No. 6 Alabama in the Iron Bowl rivalry
paragraphs: Auburn coach Alex Golesh had his players thinking about Alabama in March. He set aside part of spring practice for the rivalry known as the Iron Bowl, and the Tigers played “Dixieland Delight" — the song that will blare through Bryant-Denny Stadium to start the fourth quarter Saturday night.
That's how much this Southeastern Conference series means to the program that has been on the losing end the last six years.
Auburn (7-4, 4-4 SEC) will try to end the skid and ruin sixth-ranked Alabama's chances of making the league title game and potentially earning a first-round bye in the College Football Playoff.
“The reason why you come to Auburn, the reason why I came to Auburn: to be a part of what’s coming here this week,” Golesh said.
